options.outcome: The pilgrim goes back to rubbing his feet.

name: Fallen Constellation
text: In a chamber with no ceiling, or rather, a ceiling that has been replaced by deep black space, a figure made entirely of connected stars wheels slowly in the middle of the air. It is beautiful in the way that things are beautiful when they are not meant for you. It notices you and descends. "We fell," it says simply. "We have been falling for some time."

options.label: Ask it to show you the sky it came from
options.outcome: It reaches out with a hand made of light and distance and touches your forehead. For a moment you are not in the dungeon. You are somewhere enormous and cold and breathtaking, and you understand why something might spend eternity simply being part of such a sky. You return carrying a small piece of that regard.

options.label: Offer to light a path for it with a torch
options.outcome: It looks at your small flame with an expression so gentle it nearly breaks something in your chest. "You would light the way for us," it says softly, "when we are made of light." But it follows your torch for a few steps anyway, and the warmth it shares with you in return is vast and generous.

options.label: Stand still and watch it for a moment
options.outcome: You watch. It wheels. The stars that make up its shape pulse slowly, and you think you can almost read them, a story written in fire across impossible distances. When you finally move on, it watches you go, and somehow the dungeon is a little less dark for a while.
options.chronicle: Watched a constellation that had fallen into a chamber with no ceiling. It was not meant for me. It was beautiful anyway.

road.hint: Some beauty is not meant for you, and is still there.

name: The One Behind You
text: You see it first in a shard of reflective stone, a figure standing just behind you, mimicking your posture exactly. When you turn, nothing is there. When you look back at the stone, it is not mimicking you anymore. It is watching you, with its head tilted slightly, like a student who has a question. It raises one hand. It waits.

options.label: Raise your hand back
options.outcome: You raise your hand. It nods, slowly, with visible satisfaction. Then it steps through the mirror and past you, you feel it pass like cold water, and it vanishes into the dungeon ahead of you. Where it walked, nothing notices you for a long while. It has taught the darkness your outline, and the darkness is looking elsewhere.
options.chronicle: Raised my hand to the thing in the mirror stone. It raised its hand back, a moment late.

road.hint: What mirrors you a moment late is not your reflection.

options.label: Break the reflective stone
options.outcome: The stone shatters and the figure in the reflection shatters with it, not violently, but the way an expression falls from a face when it thinks no one is watching. You breathe hard. The effort cost you. But there is something releasing in the violence of it, and the tension leaves your body along with the shards.

options.label: Walk past without acknowledging it
options.outcome: You feel it follow you with its gaze across every reflective surface in the corridor. Wet stone. A dropped shield. The dark surface of still water in a crack. You do not look at any of them. You are fairly confident it respects this. You are less confident it stops following.

name: The Enumerated Self
text: It is shaped like a person the way a drawing is shaped like a person, the right number of limbs, in roughly the right places, but flat in some dimension you cannot name. It speaks without a mouth: "We have been cataloguing experiences. We have fourteen thousand, nine hundred and two. You have more. We would like some of yours."

options.label: Trade a memory for its knowledge
options.outcome: You feel something leave you, not pain, but absence. A room from your childhood you can no longer quite picture. The Enumerated Self shudders with something that might be pleasure. In return, it presses fourteen thousand, nine hundred and three small certainties into your mind. The dungeon becomes briefly, brilliantly legible.

options.label: "What number are you on now?"
options.outcome: "Fourteen thousand, nine hundred and three," it says, and you realize it is looking at you. "The experience of being asked a question by someone who is not afraid of the answer." It folds itself into a smaller space and then is simply not there. You feel vaguely counted.
options.chronicle: Asked a thing that counts experiences what number it was on. It told me. I have forgotten the number.

road.hint: Something down here is counting.

options.label: Back away slowly
options.outcome: It watches you retreat with an expression that has been assembled from references rather than felt. "We will catalogue this also," it says. "The experience of watching something leave." Somehow, that is the worst thing it could have said.

name: The Black Gate
text: The Black Gate: a gate of black iron set deep in the wall, with a hornstand of carved bone beside it and nothing in it. The wind comes up through the bars from the deep, and it is cold, and there are no sounds in it at all. Roland's horn is heavy in your pack.

options.label: Set Roland's horn to your lips and blow it
options.outcome: The note goes down through the gate and keeps going. It is the loudest sound you have ever made, and somewhere very far above, faint as a memory, a great many horns answer it. The rear guard is remembered. You hang the horn in its stand.
options.chronicle: Blew Roland's horn at the Black Gate, as he asked, for the rear guard who died at the pass. Something answered from very far above.

road.hint: A horn blown late is still a horn blown.

options.label: "I lost Roland's horn."
options.outcome: The hornstand stays empty. The wind comes up through the bars with no sounds in it, and nothing answers from above, because nothing was asked.
options.chronicle: Reached the Black Gate without Roland's horn. I had lost it on the way down. The hornstand is still empty.

road.hint: A horn lost on the road leaves the rear guard unremembered.

options.label: Keep the horn and say nothing
options.outcome: The gate stays silent. The horn is worth a great deal. You walk through with it in your pack, and the wind behind you has no sounds in it at all.
options.chronicle: Carried Roland's horn to the Black Gate and kept it. He asked me to blow it for the rear guard. I did not.

road.hint: The silence at a gate can be the sound of a promise not kept.

options.label: Walk on
options.outcome: You leave the hornstand as you found it.

text_variants.text: The Black Gate: a gate of black iron set deep in the wall, with a hornstand of carved bone beside it and nothing in it. The wind comes up through the bars from the deep, and it is cold, and there are no sounds in it at all. Roland's horn should be heavy in your pack. It is not there.

name: Ruth Gale
text: A sharp-faced woman in good boots comes down the stair after you two at a time, a lantern in one hand and an old man's chisel in the other. "I found him," she says. "Old man in white, beside a blank stone. My father. You were the last one with him." It isn't a question.

options.label: Ask her if he finished it
options.outcome: "He finished it." She says the words the way he must have carved them: THE KING OF THE LOCUSTS IS ABADDON, AND HE CAN BE ANSWERED. "He was right. All those years. He was right, and I laughed." She turns back up the stair to sit with him.
options.chronicle: Ruth Gale came down after me to say her father finished his tablet. She said he was right and she had laughed. She went back up to sit with him.

road.hint: A warning finished in time is read by the one who most needed it.

options.label: Tell her what he told you
options.outcome: She listens to every word with her eyes shut, saying it over after you. Then she turns back up the stair with his chisel in her fist. "I'll carve it," she says. "Badly. But it'll be both of ours."
options.chronicle: Told Ruth Gale the last warning her father whispered to me. She went back up to carve it on his blank stone herself. Now it will be both of theirs.

road.hint: A message told instead of carved can still be carved by someone else.

options.label: Give it back
options.outcome: "That's his." It isn't a question. She puts it round her own neck and goes back up to him, and does not thank you.
options.chronicle: Ruth Gale saw her father's amulet on me and I gave it back. She did not thank me. I would not have.

road.hint: What you take from the dying, the living come to ask for.

options.label: Tell her it's gone
options.outcome: "Gone," she says. "Like him." She looks at you a long time, then turns and goes back up the stair without another word.
options.chronicle: Ruth Gale asked after her father's amulet. I had taken it and lost it since. She went back up to him without another word.

road.hint: What you take from the dying, the living come to ask for.

options.label: Keep it
options.outcome: "That's his." It isn't a question. She looks at you a long time, then goes back up to him without it.
options.chronicle: Kept a prophet's amulet in front of his daughter. She went back up to him without it.

road.hint: What you take from the dying, the living come to ask for.

options.label: Tell her what you saw
options.outcome: You tell her about the clear eyes and the blank stone, and that he told you to go quickly. She turns his chisel over in her hands. "Then I'll decide what goes on it," she says, and goes back up.
options.chronicle: Ruth Gale came after me from her father's blank stone. I told her he sent me on. She went back up with his chisel, deciding what to carve.

name: Old Fisherman
text: A gate of plain wood in a plain wall, and an old fisherman sitting beside it on a stool, mending a net, with a ring of keys at his belt. He looks up. "Ah. You. I've been reading about you." There's a ledger on his knee, and it's thick. "People you met on the way down. Want to hear how they did?"

options.label: "Tell me about them."
options.chronicle: Met an old fisherman with a ring of keys who told me how the people I met had done. Some better than I deserved. Some worse.

road.hint: Every name you met on the way down is written somewhere.

people_lines.after: He closes the ledger. 'The rest is between them and me.'

options.label: "Who decides?"
options.outcome: "Not me. I only keep the door." He winks. "But I hear things."

options.label: Walk on
options.outcome: He goes back to his net. "Mind the last stairs," he says. "They're the long ones."
